newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's new inspection agency to have staff of 300.
newsitem.headline: Japan's new inspection agency to have staff of 300.

text.p: The Japanese agency that will be set up in the next fiscal year to inspect and supervise financial institutions will have a staff of over 300, Kimio Yamaguchi, director general of the Finance Ministry's banking bureau, said on Thursday.

Around 150 people at the Finance Ministry who are responsible for inspecting financial institutions will move to the new agency, along with staff currently working at Japan's securities watchdog, the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC), Yamaguchi said.
Additional staff will come from the Management and Coordination Agency and other government agencies, he said.
